teams.heading: Fiji have conceded 408 points in their last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games Fiji have scored 273 points, averaging 24.8 points a game. Their defensive numbers in the same window are the harder read: 37.1 points conceded a game on average. Their biggest win in that span was a 45-29 home victory over Canada in September, in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: Paul Williams says England's pack is under-appreciated after Australia win
teams.body: Rugby World columnist Paul Williams argues England's players are under-rated after the 45-22 win over Australia in the Nations Championship, a performance he says drew a tepid response. Japan are next up on Saturday. He singles out the tight five as an industrial-level unit, names back-rower Ben Earl as the top carrier across the competition so far, and praises fly-half Fin Smith's close passing.

teams.heading: Galthié recalls Alldritt at No. 8 after almost a year out
teams.body: Grégory Alldritt returns to the starting side for Friday's clash with South Africa, wearing the No. 8 shirt after almost a year out of favour with head coach Fabien Galthié. Galthié has picked him to counter the Springboks' forward power, and the La Rochelle forward was left out of this year's Six Nations. Planet Rugby's winners-and-losers verdict on the team names Maxime Lucu a winner, back at scrum-half with Antoine Dupont moving to fly-half. Romain Ntamack, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos are all out injured, leaving Lucu with the nine shirt.

lead.why: Alldritt's return to the France pack is a fresh selection story, and Dupont at fly-half was already covered in Tuesday's edition.

teams.heading: Joey Carbery bids for Ireland's No. 10 shirt after missing Farrell's squad
teams.body: The Leinster fly-half wants the Test number 10 jersey, telling the Ireland Rugby Social, "It's what I want." Carbery, who won the last of his 37 caps against Fiji in November 2022, has made just two starts since rejoining Leinster from Bordeaux-Begles. He missed Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's latest squad, but has been included in Mark Sexton's Ireland XV panel for next week's match against Fiji 'A' in Cork. He calls it "a foot back in the door of the Irish system and the way they play."

teams.heading: Diego Dominguez calls Italy timid against South Africa, hopes to see Allan
teams.body: Former Italy and Argentina fly-half Diego Dominguez, now a Sky Sport pitchside pundit, judged Italy timid, especially in the first half, after the 7-66 defeat to South Africa. He said the Springboks could put 40-50 points on anyone, and Italy were limited to watching their opponents. Dominguez thinks prop Danilo Fischetti and back-rower Ross Vintcent could find a place straight away against Argentina, and hopes to see fly-half Tommaso Allan, whose kicking he rates as the best in the squad.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about Italy on the shortlist; #2 and #3 have already been reported, and #4 and #5 are background.

teams.heading: RUCK's hypothetical odds put Ronan O'Gara among Gregor Townsend's 10 possible successors
teams.body: RUCK has ranked 10 candidates to succeed Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend, whose contract runs to the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. These are hypothetical odds rather than bookmaker prices, and no official shortlist has been announced. Ronan O'Gara, the former Ireland fly-half, is the 33/1 outsider, but he extended his La Rochelle contract to 2031 in September and there is no indication he is pursuing the job. Former Scotland lock Jim Hamilton has also thrown his support behind Mike Blair.

teams.heading: Aaron Wainwright set to miss All Blacks test; Taine Basham poised
teams.body: Taine Basham looks poised to get his chance in the back row against New Zealand on Saturday, with Aaron Wainwright set to miss the match. The Cardiff No 8 has 17 Wales caps, the last won against England in 2024, and WalesOnline argues he offers the explosive ball-carrying that Wales have lacked over the past 12 months, a gap the 28-21 win over Japan last Saturday did little to close. He was player of the match in the 29-28 win over Australia in 2021.

teams.heading: Julián Montoya out of Italy clash after HIA; Contepomi adds Bosch, Bernasconi
teams.body: Captain Julián Montoya, who left early against Ireland in Dublin, is out for 12 days under HIA protocols and misses Saturday's test in Genoa. Replacement Leonel Oviedo also went through HIA assessments, and his fitness remains unclear. Head coach Felipe Contepomi's two new hookers, Bosch, last capped in 2021, and Bernasconi, on three caps, may both make the 23, while uncapped Tobías Wade is looking for a first cap at fullback.

teams.heading: Ryan Lonergan defends Joseph Suaalii after Chris Ashton's 'unfair' criticism
teams.body: Wallabies scrum-half Ryan Lonergan has defended winger Joseph Suaalii against Chris Ashton, the former England winger, who told the BBC that the ex-rugby league star did not look like an international union player. Lonergan said Suaalii had been given few chances in the 45-22 defeat at Twickenham, and that Australia's problems were on the inside. "I think that's probably a little bit unfair on 'Su.'" He added that the collision battle was the main point from the team's defensive review ahead of Sunday's Scotland match.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones says Japan will seek chaos and upset at Twickenham
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones is drawing on Italy's example, who beat England in March for the first time in 33 attempts, and wants Saturday's Test at Allianz Stadium to turn into chaos. Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, he said: "We're massive underdogs," and argued Japan must disrupt England, get the crowd booing and let the pressure build. Japan have lost all six previous Tests against England, most recently 54-19 two years ago.

lead.why: A fresh Japan-side angle from Eddie Jones on his plan for England, not a rehash of the fly-half or injury stories already run.

teams.heading: Will Jordan has minor tear, Neil Barnes unsure of Wales availability
teams.body: Winger Will Jordan picked up a suspected hamstring injury in the second half against Scotland at Murrayfield, and All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes has not ruled him out of the Wales match. "It's a minor tear, but it depends how quickly it starts to heal this week," Barnes said, with scans set to guide the decision. Jordie Barrett is also a doubt after failing a head injury assessment, and the All Blacks are set to make multiple changes for the game at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

lead.why: A new injury update on the All Blacks' record try-scorer, with Wales availability in doubt, is the freshest team news in the pack.

teams.heading: Mark Andrews hails Siya Kolisi as the Springboks' most successful captain
teams.body: Former Springboks lock Mark Andrews, a 1995 World Cup winner, told the Big Men Talking podcast that head coach Rassie Erasmus picked Siya Kolisi as captain because "he was the best captain that he had". Andrews recalled Kolisi's humility at a jersey handover, when the young skipper showed real respect for an older player. Kolisi has since led the Boks to 58 Test wins, the most by any Springboks captain, after passing John Smit's 54 earlier this year.
